In modern vehicles there are many systems controlled by a dedicated ECU that interacts with those of other
systems
ControlVehicle’s

slides.title: (Engine Control Module) ECM
slides.body:
The ECM is the ECU dedicated to engine control and its
main tasks are :
o Combustion control
o Management of the requested power
o Emission control
(Engine Control Module)ECM

slides.title: Calibration Software and
slides.body:
o SOFTWARE: the software of the ECM is composed by a firmware and an application; the application
contains all the algorithms and the engine control strategies. It is normally supplied with default
settings (calibrations)
o CALIBRATION: the calibration procedure is the operation through which the software is customized
for different applications (this makes it possible to use the same software for different applications)
CalibrationSoftware and

slides.title: Production ECU Development ECU Vs
slides.body:
There are two different types of ECUs :
o Opened or development
o Closed or production
The main difference between the two types is in the number of installed memories
Production ECUDevelopment ECU Vs

slides.title: ECU Production
slides.body:
The production unit has 3 memories:
o ECU flash: processor memory that is programmed with
the complete sw
o ECU Ram: supporting memory
o EEPROM: part of the memory on which the control unit
saves data before switching off
ECUProduction

slides.title: ECU Development
slides.body:
The development unit has 4 memories :
o ECU flash and EEPROM are the same of the production
one
o ETK flash: additional memory that stores a page with
calibrations during ECU shutdown
o ETK Ram: volatile memory that contains two calibration
pages ''Working page'' and ''Reference page'' with the
possibility to switch from one to the other on the fly

ETK Ram memory

slides.title: IN tegrated Ca libration and Measurement System
slides.body:
INtegrated Calibration and Measurement System INCA
INCA is a diagnostic tool that allows you to :
o Read the variables of the software present on the ECM (Engine Control
Module)
o Change the calibration parameters
o Acquire the results of a measurement/calibration
o Download the sw on the ECU memory

slides.title: Hardware ETAS
slides.body:
INCA uses some specific interfaces produced by ETAS to communicate with the ECUs; below there
are the images of two ETAS hardware :
HardwareETAS
ES 592 ES 581

slides.title: ES592 ETAS
slides.body:
The ES592 interface represents a more complete version of
the ETAS peripheral devices as it allows connection with the
development ECU either via an ETK cable or via a CAN
network (CCP connection) and with CAN production control
units
ES592ETAS -

slides.title: ES581 ETAS
slides.body:
The ES581 interface represents a simpler version of the
ETAS peripherals as it allows connection to the ECU (both
production and development) only via CAN network (CCP
connection).
With this hardware it’s possible also to monitor the CAN
Network by the CAN-Monitoring functionality.

slides.body:
The main functionalities of INCA are:
o Calibration management
o Data acquisition
o ECU flash programming
o Measure analysis

slides.title: Configuration INCA
Configuration INCA
slides.body:
The creation of a Top
folder is the first step
to connect INCA with
any ECU.
ConfigurationINCA -
Right button of the mouse
on ‘’Database Objects’’ , and
select
Add -> Top Folder

slides.title: Configuration INCA
slides.body:
After the creation of the
Top Folder, the user has
to create a Workspace.
The workspace will
contain all the
information necessary to
connect INCA with the
ECU
ConfigurationINCA -
Click on Add Workspace
icon on the toolbar
Point the mouse on the created folder
and, by clicking on the right button,
choose Add Workspace

slides.title: Configuration INCA
slides.body:
INCA can communicate with an ECU only with a compatible software. In this way it’s necessary the import
of the ECU software in INCA. A software compatible with ASAP protocol is composed in two main parts:
o Base software: .A2L file;
o Dataset of the calibration: HEX, csv, s19, srec,…
ConfigurationINCA -
Point the mouse on the created folder, click
on the right button and choose Add Ecu
Project and then follow the instructions to
associate the A2L and HEX files
- A2L: file containing the detailed description of
the elements of the sw, including physical
characteristics of the parameters and the
memory address whre it is located
- HEX, csv, s19, srec: file containing the
calibration dataset (the file format depends on
the supplier)

slides.title: Configuration INCA
slides.body:
INCA needs of a physical connection
between host PC and ECU; user has to
select the hardware device for
communication; the selected hardware
depends of the communication channel
(ETK, CCP,…).
User has to associate (in the Workspace) the
software and the hardware for the connection
with the ECU
ConfigurationINCA -
In hardware section, click with the mouse on
Hardware Icon to select the device
Select the workspace, in Project/Device
section, press on “+” and add the software.

slides.title: Configuration INCA
slides.body:
Hardware section: in this section the
user associates the connected
hardware to the Project and so the
workspace.
ConfigurationINCA -
Clicking on the magnifier icon starts
the search for the hardware interface
When the hardware has been
identified and associated correctly, we

slides.title: Reference Page Working Page Vs
slides.body:
INCA allows to pass in real time from the
Working page to the Reference Page.
The Reference Page is an only readable
memory page; in the Reference Page
there are the calibration provided from
the software supplier.
The Working page is a writable memory
page and the user can carry out the
modification to the calibration; the
modification of the calibration could be
necessary for analysis procedure.
Reference page (RP): default calibration
dataset contained in the sw supplied by
the supplier
Working page (WP): dataset that can be
modified during the development phase;
useful to adapt the software for a specific
application
Reference PageWorking Page Vs

The calibration environment allows

slides.title: configuration Experiment
slides.body:
The user has to select the variables
(measurement and calibration) that
he needs for analysis and
calibration tasks.
The user has to click on the
Variable selection icon for variable
selection.
configurationExperiment

slides.title: configuration Experiment
slides.body:
In the variable selection window
there are all the calibration and
measurement variable of the
software.
Usually the supplier builds the
software using many software
modules; each variable is a part of a
specific module.
The user can choose between
measurement (e.g. raw data of a
sensor or command value of an
actuator) or calibration variables
(e.g. Torque Map, enabling of a
diagnosis,…).
For each measurement variable, the
user can choose the acquisition
raster.
configurationExperiment
Measurement
variables
Calibration
variables
Acquisition raster

slides.title: configuration Experiment
slides.body:
The user has to start the
communication to check in real time
the values of all selected software
variables.
There are three commands:
o Start visualization – the user
checks in real time the trend of
software variables;
o Start recording – the user checks
and records in real time the
software variables;
o Stop measuring – the user stops
the visualization and the
recording.

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
INCA allows to reprogram the
control unit either by overwriting the
whole software or by replacing the
variables dataset only.
The Manage Memory pages section
allows to perform the following
operations:
o Download
o Copy
o Flash programming
o Upload
flashingECU

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
The Download operation allows
to download the INCA database
on the control unit Working
page Ram
flashingECU

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
Copy operation allows to copy
the Working page on the
Reference page and vice versa.
This operation could be useful
in case of restoring of a working
page.
flashingECU

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
The Upload operation allows to
retrieve the Working page and
the Reference page from the
memory of the control unit and
to import them into the INCA
database.
flashingECU

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
The operation of Flash
Programming allows to
download the software and/or
the calibration on the
permanent memory of the
control unit.
The operation of Flash
Programming requires the
configuration of the ProF which
represents the configuration file
of the control unit
flashingECU

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
The user has to follow the
step reported in the image
for ECU flashing.
flashingECU
1. Select Flash programming and
press Do it
2. INCA open the ProF setting
window; click on the button Configure
3. INCA open the ProF
configuration window

slides.title: flashing ECU
slides.body:
After the selection of the
ProF, the last step is the
starting of flashing
procedure; the user has to
press the button OK.
INCA starts to erase the
EEPROM and to
download the new
software.
INCA will advise when the
procedure finishes.

Calibration Data Manager CDM
CDM is used to process calibration data sets in INCA. In particular, it allows to
manage several datasets simultaneously through the Copy, List, Compare and
Merge functions; it’s possible also an export of the calibration data in Excel or
ASCII format.

slides.title: Measure Data Analyzer MDA:
slides.body:
MDA allows the post-
processing analysis; the
user can check only the
variable that has been
acquired in INCA.
Measure Data AnalyzerMDA:
Once open the program we
choose the file previously
acquired with INCA (in .dat
format). Selecting File will open
a window to choose the .dat file
to use

slides.title: Measure Data Analyzer MDA:
slides.body:
Once the .dat file is open,
the user chooses the
variables to display from the
window; the user chooses
also the display mode.
The more comfortable way
to perform the post
processing analysis is using
an oscilloscope: the user
has to use the function
<new_oscilloscope>.
To display the selected
variables more clearly, the
user can highlight them and
can select the value
Distribute Uniformly.
